crossRefs.note: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!
I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
“Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
“Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
“Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
Put me in remembrance. Let us plead together. Declare your case, that you may be justified.
Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of…
For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom…

translations.web: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.
translations.bsb: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
translations.kjv: Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.
translations.asv: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.
